title: Keyboard, touch and drag access
description: Interactive tasks need usable targets and appropriate input alternatives.
guidance: Check keyboard operation, target size and spacing, and an alternative to dragging when applicable. Keep focus visible and return it at the end of transient interactions.
verification: Complete the key tasks with touch and keyboard on the rendered artifact. Measure relevant targets and check the applicable WCAG exceptions.
counterexamples: An inline link can qualify for a target-size exception. Some native or essential interactions have different applicable criteria.

title: Typographic detail and stability
description: Type needs to remain readable and aligned as labels, numbers and available space change.
guidance: Review type scale, optical spacing, line length and wrapping. Use width reservation, text-box trim, underline offsets, fluid sizing or truncation only where they improve the measured state.
verification: Compare the affected lines or controls at narrow and wide widths, with long translations and changing content.
counterexamples: A readable long title may be more useful than a uniform card height. Deliberate editorial variation can support the composition.

title: Responsive layout and safe areas
description: Content and primary actions need room on narrow, short and changing viewports.
guidance: Inspect device safe areas, browser chrome, zoom and keyboard open states. Check overflow, clipping, layering and whether sticky controls cover important content.
verification: Use the real page and target inputs at relevant widths and heights. Repeat with the keyboard open, zoom increased and long or localized text.
counterexamples: A map, timeline or dense data table can require intentional horizontal navigation while keeping its controls and surrounding content accessible.

title: Public route discovery and sharing
description: A public page should be identifiable and usable when opened, indexed or shared.
guidance: Check distinct page titles and descriptions, canonical URLs, social preview images, internal links, index directives and the actual not-found response for the intended public routes.
verification: Inspect the rendered metadata, canonical destinations and public navigation. Check status and index intent for visible routes and a missing route.
counterexamples: Authenticated workspace routes, duplicated language-neutral previews and temporary staging pages have different indexing and metadata goals.

title: Public business and support information
description: Visitors need accurate contact, location and support information to make a decision.
guidance: Verify business identity, response-time promises and relevant FAQs. Provide current directions and matching local structured data where an actual customer-facing location exists.
verification: Compare the information with the actual offer and information supplied by the operator. Walk navigation and contact paths.
counterexamples: An online-only tool may have no location to visit. Existing support documentation may answer questions without a separate FAQ.

title: Product notices and consent flows
description: User-facing disclosures and choices need to match the actual feature, data flow and market.
guidance: Verify which privacy, cookie, AI, terms, renewal, cancellation or refund disclosures apply. Check choices in forms and analytics, consent withdrawal and marketing unsubscribe where relevant.
verification: Compare notices and controls with actual supported flows, SDKs and provider data handling. Record legal applicability that still needs authoritative review.
counterexamples: A tracker-free site, non-renewing purchase or purely local demo can have different disclosure and consent needs.

title: Deployed transport and origin policies
description: TLS, cross-origin policies and response headers need to match the deployed topology and trust boundaries.
guidance: Review HTTPS, CORS for sensitive responses, and security headers at the application and authorized edge configuration. Document any intentional public access.
verification: Review the relevant app, host and proxy configuration or recorded deployment evidence. Keep environment-specific gaps visible.
counterexamples: A deliberately public, credential-free endpoint may allow a broad origin policy. Loopback development traffic can have distinct transport settings.

title: Upload validation and serving
description: Uploaded files cross ownership, storage and content-handling boundaries.
guidance: Apply relevant type, size and ownership constraints before processing. Verify safe rendering, storage permissions, serving policy and deletion through the file lifecycle.
verification: Trace upload, processing, download and deletion source. Use approved local fixtures to verify expected product behavior where supported.
counterexamples: An intentionally public asset library has a different access policy from private user attachments.

title: Short-form explanation and demonstration
description: A short explainer needs a clear focal action and legible supporting information at the moment it is discussed.
guidance: Use real product states or sourced examples, clear before and after states, and selective annotation. Keep captions, sources and useful labels within the viewing safe area and time them to the spoken point.
verification: Watch the actual export at its intended size and speed. Inspect key beats for visible evidence, caption position, read time and continuity.
counterexamples: A quiet documentary sequence can hold a verified image or diagram without labels when that supports comprehension.
